claim_boundary: The external evidence supports total open interest as a market-participation and risk-state variable, not as a directional position measure or an established BTC return predictor. The positive-growth long/cash rule is one transparent falsifiable risk-regime hypothesis built on BTC's positive long-run risk premium; it is not a literature replication or a proven alpha claim.
causal_hypothesis: A weekly increase in total regulated CME Bitcoin futures open interest may identify deeper participation and risk-bearing capacity that makes BTC's positive risk premium more investable, while falling participation may identify a less resilient state.
economic_hypothesis: A full-capital BTC long-or-zero-yield-cash policy using one causally lagged weekly total-open-interest growth sign may preserve sufficient BTC upside while improving fee- and adverse-slippage-adjusted drawdown and Calmar versus matched buy-and-hold.

frozen_feature.availability_rationale: Day seven at 00:00 UTC is conservatively after the frozen three-to-six-calendar-day release window without reconstructing unsealed historical receipt times.

primary_sources.title: CFTC Commitments of Traders Explanatory Notes
primary_sources.use: Official semantics: open interest is the total of contracts not yet offset or otherwise closed, aggregate long open interest equals aggregate short open interest, and weekly change is the difference from the previous report. This proves participation identity but explicitly does not prove bullish direction.

primary_sources.title: The impacts of futures trading on volatility and volatility asymmetry of Bitcoin returns
primary_sources.use: Supportive risk-state prior: the published study reports that unexpected futures open interest covaries negatively with Bitcoin volatility in the long run, while not establishing this weekly sign rule or positive subsequent returns.

primary_sources.title: The COVID-19 pandemic, volatility, and trading behavior in the bitcoin futures market
primary_sources.use: Adversarial regime prior: the study reports unclear pre-pandemic relations and that increased belief dispersion during pandemic stress reduced Bitcoin-futures returns while raising volume and volatility.

independence_and_duplicate_boundary.distinct_from_closed_participant_positio: Closed CFTC families used net long-minus-short changes of specific participant classes. This family uses only market-level total open interest and never inspects participant direction.
independence_and_duplicate_boundary.direction_limitation: Because aggregate long open interest equals aggregate short open interest, the factor is a participation regime, not a bullish positioning signal. Passing requires economic drawdown and Calmar evidence; positive total return alone is insufficient.
independence_and_duplicate_boundary.shared_source_risk: All CFTC families reuse the same CME TFF weekly archive, release clock and BTC corpus. Market-level identity is a distinct mechanism hypothesis, not independent data-source replication.
independence_and_duplicate_boundary.prohibited_reclassification: A failed result cannot be rescued by adding price trend, basis, funding, volume, trader category, percentile, level or interaction filters.

adversarial_prior: Total open interest is directionless because every open long has an open short; growth can represent hedging, arbitrage or leverage crowding rather than bullish informed demand.
CME contract adoption and institutional access trended upward during the sample, so an open-interest growth rule can inherit a calendar or adoption trend without independent predictive value.
Pandemic evidence shows the relationship between open interest, returns and volatility can change materially across stress regimes.
The volatility paper decomposes expected and unexpected daily activity and does not establish a weekly raw-growth return signal, fee-adjusted PnL or drawdown improvement.
The CFTC report is weekly and conservatively lagged; a usable factor may miss much of a fast BTC move and create long cash intervals or terminal inventory concentration.
stop_conditions: Stop DATA_REJECT before factor evaluation if any archive hash, exact contract row count, ordered field identity, Tuesday report date, exact seven-day predecessor, ION exclusion, numeric grammar, open-interest change identity or BTC H1 corpus identity fails.
Stop NO_CANDIDATE before strategy economics if any frozen Design or Validation predictive sample, median, rank-test or concentration gate fails.

If predictive gates pass, stop NO_CANDIDATE unless the single primary passes every frozen normal/stress Design, Validation, annual breadth, drawdown, Calmar, upside, concentration, holding and terminal-inventory economic gate.

Do not invert direction or scan open-interest level, raw change, percentage threshold, z-score, percentile, smoothing, lag, horizon, report timing, position size, leverage or shorting after factor or outcome access.
Do not add BTC trend, basis, funding, volume, participant categories, macro, on-chain, volatility or DRA interactions to rescue a failed result.
Do not open post-2024 BTC outcomes. Any historical pass remains REPORTED_NOT_ACTIVATED and requires independently sealed OOS.
